- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (especially in 30d horizon), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor (e.g., 0.95) to subsequent forecasts.
- In periods with high volatility or low sentiment, model underestimates downward moves; increase forecast sensitivity to recent lows.
- If sentiment turns from negative to positive within 5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to capture sentiment shift.
- For 30d forecasts, model tends to underestimate mid-term mean reversion; add 1–2% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to avoid flat forecasts.
